exposure: high Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) scores
cohort: 676 English or Spanish-speaking women ≥18 years who had prenatal care for a singleton gestation and delivered by cesarean at ≥36 weeks within a tertiary center during 2017
finding: Higher antenatal Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) scores are associated with increased pain scores and opioid use during postpartum hospitalization following cesarean section.
mod_finding: This study did not examine mode of delivery as a predictor of pain but found that women with major depressive symptoms reported higher pain scores and used more opioids after cesarean delivery.
